query: FeNiCrCoCu is considered promising for high-heat wear-resistant use and is suitable for thin-film applications; because bulk preparation is expensive, applying it as a coating on a conventional metal is more practical. Earlier studies reported improved wear or mechanical performance from high-entropy-alloy coatings on Al, Ni, and titanium-alloy substrates, and simulations of FeNiCrCoCu on Cu indicated that sliding speed affects tangential and normal forces. Other work associated composition and grain size with changes in wear damage. However, most prior studies examined a limited operating regime or the properties of the alloys themselves rather than the overall wear resistance of coatings under varied thermal conditions. Subject to retaining FeNiCrCoCu as a coating on a Cu matrix, what single intervention could improve its overall wear resistance during sliding across varied thermal and contact regimes? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its causal mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to an unchanged coating in matched tests, the boundaries within which it should hold, supporting evidence from the introduction, and an experiment with a clear rejection criterion for both the predicted outcome and the proposed mechanism.

generation.hypothesis: Reducing the grain size of the FeNiCrCoCu coating on a Cu matrix will improve its overall wear resistance during sliding across varied thermal and contact regimes.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu coating on a Cu matrix
generation.intervention: Reducing the grain size of the FeNiCrCoCu coating
generation.mechanism: Fine grain size provides higher surface strength and hardness, which improves wear resistance. Under friction heat, coarse grain samples soften more easily, causing their oxide layers to fracture and leading to increased wear.
generation.boundary: Within the range of grain sizes that can be achieved through processing techniques
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between grain size and wear resistance may depend on other factors such as the specific processing technique and the testing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu coatings with different grain sizes under varied thermal and contact regimes
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear resistance of the coating with reduced grain size is not improved, then the hypothesis is falsified

Question: How does grain size influence the tribological behavior, wear mechanisms, and wear resistance of CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloys under varying normal loads and sliding speeds?. System: CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloy (HEA) with fine grain (FG, ~2.9 μm) and coarse grain (CG, ~63.4 μm) microstructures. Processing: Arc-melting of pure metals followed by drop-casting into a copper mold, forging at 1000 °C, cold rolling (80% reduction), and annealing at 800 °C for 30 min (FG) or 1000 °C for 60 min (CG). Test conditions: Reciprocating sliding friction against a 10 mm Si3N4 ball under dry conditions at room temperature; normal loads of 5 N and 30 N; sliding speeds of 1, 5, and 10 mm/s; sliding time of 1200 s.
